def:ncg-grand-tensor.title: Finite Renewal Grand Tensor
def:ncg-grand-tensor.note: Encoded. `GrandTensor` bundles the complete finite-future predictive law (whose quotient is the future-minimal carrier Z^min = PredictiveSystem.MinimalCarrier) with a represented generator family gen : Γ → Matrix M M ℂ on a finite support-minimal carrier; from it are derived the represented history algebra A^hist = StarAlgebra.adjoin ℂ (range gen) (eq:ncg-history-algebra), the represented word operators [w] (wordOp, multiplicative under concatenation), the normalized regular trace τ_reg = normalizedRegularTrace A^hist (eq:ncg-grand-regular-trace), the word-Gram kernel K_X(v,w) = τ_reg([v]^*[w]) (wordGram, eq:ncg-word-gram) and its depth-r layers K_{X,r} (wordGramLevel). Disclosed: the tomographic construction of the generator family from the intervention tables is not formalized (gen is data), and positivity of the Gram kernel is not proved (it is a remark in the paper, not part of the definition).

prop:ncg-grand-tensor-reconstruction.title: Canonical finite Grand-Tensor reconstruction
prop:ncg-grand-tensor-reconstruction.note: Proved in the precise form the paper's proof establishes. (i) universal surjection from every reachable deterministic realization onto Z^min intertwining branch laws and occurring updates (existing, re-bundled). (ii) Support-minimal realization stacks N, N' of the same positive process Gram (N^H N = N'^H N') carrying represented operators implementing the same word shifts are related by a unitary Ω with Ω N = N' and T' = Ω T Ω^* (exists_unitary_intertwiner, from gram_unitary and intertwine_of_surjective); unitarily conjugate generator families generate history algebras identified by the represented *-isomorphism x ↦ U x U^* (conjEquiv, historyAlgebra_conj). (iii) The normalized regular trace is transported by that isomorphism and the whole word-Gram hierarchy K_{X,r} is invariant (normalizedRegularTrace_conjEquiv, wordGram_conj, wordGramLevel_conj). (iv) grand_tensor_reconstruction bundles (i)-(iii) for a Grand Tensor and its conjugate presentation, including equality of the minimal carriers. Disclosed gap: the passage from 'complete operational statistics' (tomographically complete intervention tables) to the positive process matrices is informal in the paper and is not formalized; uniqueness is proved from equal process Gram data onward.

thm:summary-finite.title: Spectralization, Dirac ambiguity, and calibrated image
thm:summary-finite.note: Aggregate of thm:finite-spectralization, prop:no-scale, thm:commutant-fibre and thm:essential-image; see those records for the scoped renderings (coordinate packet whose Leibniz/right-linearity/reversal-intertwining fields are hypotheses, abstract linear-constraint commutant model, and image equalities rendered as existence certificates plus the exact strict criterion and Toeplitz properness witness).

thm:summary-metric.title: Independent metric reconstruction and stable compact-spin convergence
thm:summary-metric.note: Partial: clause (i) is proved (graph Hodge-Dirac square/commutator identities and uniform convergence of the A3 Connes distance to the flat torus quotient metric); for (iv) only the abstract collectively-compact strong-plus-adjoint to norm-resolvent upgrade is proved. Missing: (ii) relation-adapted cellular completion and its compact limit, (iii) covariant Wilson species/graph estimates, the atlas-based norm-resolvent theorem, and (v) the global metric head.
thm:summary-metric.plan: Aggregate of five clauses; (i) is proved (CanonicalGraphSpectralizationExact, A3ConnesFlatUniformConvergenceExact). (ii)-(v) depend on the cellular completion continuum limit, the Wilson species/Garding estimates (thm:supp-general-Wilson-ellipticity), the atlas norm-resolvent theorem (thm:supp-compact-spin-resolvent) and the global metric head (thm:supp-global-metric), all of which need unbounded self-adjoint operators, Sobolev/Rellich compactness and Riemannian geodesic approximation absent from Mathlib. Only the abstract collectively-compact step (OperatorLimits/CollectivelyCompactStrongAdjointToNorm.lean) exists; cannot be assembled before those components.

thm:summary-universality.title: Universality fibres and coarse graining
thm:summary-universality.note: Partial: (i) the current fibre (open conductance box in ker B, dimension b_1, entropy zero iff j=0) is proved but not the modular-class recovery of the generator; (ii) only Hankel-rank minimal realization and unique similarity (no Stieltjes measure classification, no Pontryagin index); (iii) only the Z/2 special case (holonomy separates H^1(Gamma;Z/2)); (iv) only b_1 monotonicity and a lumpable entropy split; (v) nothing.
thm:summary-universality.plan: Aggregate: (i) needs thm:supp-graph-realization + thm:supp-nonlinear-Hodge (finite, feasible), (ii) needs the operator-valued Stieltjes dilation (con:supp-Naimark-tail, hard) and the Pontryagin realization (thm:supp-complete-rational-Krein, hard), (iii) needs general-G monodromy classification (thm:supp-marked-bundle, medium), (iv) the coarse-graining functors (thm:supp-fibre-RG, hard), (v) the stratified exhaustion theorems (hard). Assemble only after the components; the finite graph/monodromy parts could be stated as a partial packet from FiniteGraphSpectralUniversalityFibreExact.lean and NCG/Graph/SignedCover.lean.

def:finite-real-differential.title: Finite real differential datum
def:finite-real-differential.note: FiniteRealDifferentialDatum n A K := {P : Packet n A K // P.IsStarBimoduleDerivation} bundles the Hilbert A-bimodule K (commuting star-adjoint left/right actions), the antiunitary involution C (reverse_inner, reverse_involutive) and delta with delta(1)=0, Leibniz and C delta(a)=delta(a^*) as named field lemmas; the reversal law C(a xi b) = b^* C(xi) a^* is reverse_bimodule (derived from reverse_left/reverse_right and commutation of the actions). The retained carrier 'only the bimodule generated by delta(A)' is sourceMinimalCarrier = range T_delta with the source-minimal quotient isomorphism sourceMinimalEquiv, and the induced derivation satisfies T_delta(d_u a) = delta a (universalFactor_differential), in particular T_delta(d_u 1) = 0. Scoped: A is a normed complex star-algebra with a finite basis (the compiler Packet's basis field).

thm:finite-spectralization.title: Finite spectralization
thm:finite-spectralization.note: Proved in orthonormal coordinates: D Hermitian and odd, J antiunitary with J^2=1, JD=DJ, J gamma=gamma J, opposite representation R_b (+) rho(b), order-zero and first-order identities, the commutator block formula and the exact norm identity ||[D,pi(a)]||=||B_a|| for a=a^*. Scoped: the Lean Packet takes as structural hypotheses the properties the paper derives from Definition finite-real-differential (Leibniz block identity, right-linearity of B_a, reversal intertwining J_1 d = d J_0), and faithfulness of pi is not stated.

prop:no-scale.title: No algebra-and-trace determination of the Dirac scale
prop:no-scale.note: D -> sD and L_D -> sL_D are proved literally for s>0 on the coordinate packet (scaling the differential block, which is the canonical identification of the one-form carriers); the distance law d -> s^{-1} d is proved for the attained finite Connes variational maximum between two linear functionals.

prop:finite-CQMS.title: Compact quantum metric-space structure
prop:finite-CQMS.note: Proved, with the following disclosed scoping. The finite algebra is realised as a *-subalgebra S of Matrix H H C (H finite, nonempty) with the inclusion as (faithful) representation, so the paper's ||a|| is the Euclidean operator norm; D is any matrix (Hermitian for the star identity); the kernel hypothesis Ker partial = C1 is taken in the form: a in S with [D,a] = 0 is a complex multiple of 1 (this is thm:finite-spectralization's characterisation, cf. FiniteRealEvenSpectralizationExact.Packet.connesMetricFinite_iff_kernelConstants). The real order-unit space A_sa is selfAdjointPart S, L_D = lipSA D S = ||[D, a]||, tau = normalized trace; the abstract package LipData is instantiated (lipData) with continuity of L_D proved, and the kernel condition transported to A_sa (kernelConstants: the scalar is real). finite_cqms_matrix gives the Poincare-Lip inequality, finiteness of mk_{L_D} on states with mk <= C||phi - psi|| <= 2C, |phi(a) - psi(a)| <= L_D(a) mk, and the bi-Lipschitz comparison with the dual norm; finite_cqms_matrix_tendsto: mk-convergence of states iff norm convergence, and tendsto_iff_forall_tendsto_apply: norm convergence iff pointwise (weak-*) convergence in the finite-dimensional dual, so mk_{L_D} induces the weak-* topology. States are modelled as normalized contractive functionals on A_sa (LipData.IsState); isState_of_nonneg proves that every positive normalized functional (phi(1) = 1, phi >= 0 on positive semidefinite elements) is such a state, so the paper's state space S(A) is covered (the converse inclusion, standard in C*-algebras, is not needed for the claims and not proved). Leibniz and star identities: finite_cqms_matrix_leibniz_star. Converse: if Ker partial contains a non-scalar self-adjoint element, two (genuinely positive) vector states have unbounded supremum eq:finite-state-metric (finite_cqms_matrix_converse_not_bddAbove), i.e. infinite distance.

prop:austere-zero-mode.title: Unit zero-mode of the austere Hodge construction
prop:austere-zero-mode.note: Proved in the orthonormal coordinates of thm:finite-spectralization (FiniteRealEvenSpectralizationExact.Packet): with unitZeroForm = Sum.elim unitVector 0 the coordinate vector of (1,0), the Hodge-Dirac block matrix dirac = fromBlocks 0 differential^H differential 0 satisfies dirac *ᵥ unitZeroForm = 0, hence det dirac = 0 and dirac is not a unit (never invertible). Scoped hypotheses, disclosed: the unit clause delta(1)=0 of def:finite-real-differential enters as differential *ᵥ unitVector = 0 (the coordinate packet does not record how unitVector sits relative to differential; at the compiler level the same clause is FiniteRealDifferentialDatum.delta_one / universalFactor_differential_one), and unitVector ≠ 0 (the coordinate vector of 1 ≠ 0). The 'more generally' sentence on the compatible-commutant ambiguity is thm:commutant-fibre (already proved, complete_solution_fibre).

thm:commutant-fibre.title: Exact Dirac commutant fibre
thm:commutant-fibre.note: Proved in an abstract finite-dimensional real inner-product model: the derivation X -> [X,pi(.)] and the grading/reality sign equations are arbitrary R-linear constraint maps, the compatible anchor space is their common kernel, the solution set is the affine fibre D + c, the centered point D - P_c D is the unique minimum-norm representative, and q = dim c real coordinates are necessary and sufficient. Scoped: the identification of the abstract kernel with the concrete self-adjoint commutant c_S is the instantiation, not a separate lemma.

thm:essential-image.title: Calibrated marked image and norm-compatible essential image
thm:essential-image.note: The three lines are rendered as: (1) every coordinate finite (real even) spectral packet has a marked realization retaining the calibrated unitary germ i U'(0)=D and the source-minimal commutator Gram; (2) every SpectralTriple with compact resolvent (no separability hypothesis needed) has finite Dirac spectral screens with strong convergence of compressions, matrix coefficients and product defects; (3) norm multiplicativity of the compressions is equivalent to two-sided quasidiagonal corner decay for any family of self-adjoint idempotents along a filter; properness is the Toeplitz number-operator/shift certificate. Scoped: the equalities EssIm = Spec are stated through these certificates rather than as category-theoretic essential images.

def:supp-renewal-graph.title: Stationary finite renewal graph
def:supp-renewal-graph.note: Bundled structure StationaryRenewalGraph V: masses m_x > 0 with sum 1, rates k_xy >= 0 for x != y (diagonal normalized to 0, since the generator sum over y != x ignores it), the mass-stationarity equation sum_y (q_xy - q_yx) = 0 for q = m k, and connectedness (ConductanceConnected) of the positive support of c = (q+q^T)/2. Derived generator L f (x) = sum_{y != x} k_xy (f y - f x) (generator_eq_sum_erase), flux q, conductance c = symmetrizedConductance q, current j = (q - q^T)/2 with c symmetric, j antisymmetric, q = c + j and sum_y j_xy = 0. StationaryRenewalGraph.spectralization discharges the hypotheses of canonical_graph_spectralization (thm:supp-graph-square), so the Hodge-Dirac carriers dirac/differential/representation of the earlier encoding attach to every such graph. Scoped: real scalars, both orientations retained via V x V.

thm:supp-graph-square.title: Renewal Hodge square and exact Lipschitz seminorm
thm:supp-graph-square.note: From positive masses, nonnegative stationary rates and connected conductance support: d^*d f = -(L f + L^dagger f) = -2 L_s f in vertex coordinates, ||[D,f]||^2 = max_x (1/m_x) sum_y c_xy |f(y)-f(x)|^2 for real f, the kernel is exactly the constants, and the resulting Connes distance on V is a metric. Scoped: real-valued vertex functions.

cth:supp-extensive-kernel.title: Extensive kernel of the one-step graph calculus
cth:supp-extensive-kernel.note: dim ker D = 2e+2-n for the block Dirac of any differential d:V->W with dim V=n, dim W=2e and dim ker d=1 (the connectedness input is taken as this hypothesis), the A3 count 11n+2, and unboundedness of these nullities (the no-compact-resolvent-limit clause is rendered as this unboundedness).

lem:supp-A3-frame.title: $A_3$ tight-frame identity
lem:supp-A3-frame.note: sum_alpha alpha alpha^T = 8 I and (1/8) sum_alpha <v,alpha>^2 = |v|^2 are proved for the explicit twelve roots (+-e_i +- e_j) of A3 written in R^3 coordinates of W_0 rather than in the R^4 hyperplane presentation.

thm:supp-A3-finite.title: Exact finite $A_3$ spectralization
thm:supp-A3-finite.note: Not attacked in this pass (the batch time went to the other four records, all now closed). Partial as before: the exact seminorm formula eq:supp-A3-Lip on the periodic A3 graph, D_h^2 = -2 L_h via the general stationary theorem, and uniform convergence L_h(F|V_h) -> ||grad F||_inf for lattice-periodic C^1 F are proved; missing: the explicit O(h ||F||_{C^2}) rate eq:supp-A3-Lip-convergence and the generator convergence L_h F -> (1/2) Delta F for C^4 F.
thm:supp-A3-finite.plan: Unchanged: two self-contained real-analysis files on Fin 3 / the A3 root system. (a) Rate: define a C^2 seminorm on lattice-periodic functions (sup of ||F||, ||DF||, ||D^2F||); along each root line t -> F(x + t h alpha) apply Mathlib taylor_mean_remainder_lagrange (as in DiscreteAnalysis/UniformFiniteDifferenceRemainderExact.lean) to get |(F(x+h alpha)-F(x))/h - alpha.grad F(x)| <= (h/2)|alpha|^2 ||D^2F||; the reverse triangle inequality in l^2(Phi_A3) plus the tight-frame identity tight_frame_energy (A3FiniteDifferenceConsistencyExact.lean) turn the root-difference energy into ||grad F(x)||^2 up to O(h), and sqrt is 1/2-Hoelder-controlled near the max, giving |L_h - ||grad F||_inf| <= C h ||F||_{C^2} after maximizing over the mesh (use A3PeriodicGraphSamplingExact.graphLipschitz_sample_sq_eq). (b) Generator: fourth-order Taylor along root lines, cancellation of odd orders by central symmetry of Phi_A3, and sum_alpha (alpha (x) alpha) : D^2F = 8 Delta F from the frame identity, giving L_h F = (1/2) Delta F + O(h^2 ||F||_{C^4}). Several days of bookkeeping; no missing infrastructure.

lem:supp-A3-compactness.title: Compactness of discrete unit-Lipschitz functions
lem:supp-A3-compactness.note: Partial: anchored discrete unit-ball functions admit 18-Lipschitz Euclidean extensions with a uniformly convergent subsequence on every closed ball; missing: the sharp limit bound |grad F| <= 1 a.e. and the W^{1,inf} identification (the Lean distance proof avoids this lemma by smoothing).
lem:supp-A3-compactness.plan: The library has an 18-Lipschitz extension with uniformly convergent subsequence (A3DiscreteUnitBallCompactnessExact.lean:exists_uniformly_convergent_extensions_on_ball) but the sharp conclusion |∇F| <= 1 a.e. in W^{1,∞} is not reachable: it needs lower semicontinuity of the A3 seminorm under uniform limits of interpolants and the W^{1,∞} = Lipschitz identification. Reformulate as 'the limit F is 1-Lipschitz for the Euclidean metric' (then |∇F| <= 1 a.e. follows from Mathlib's Rademacher theorem LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt); even so the sharp constant 1 (rather than 18) requires a new interpolation argument (the Lean distance proof deliberately avoids this lemma by smoothing).

thm:supp-A3-distance.title: Renewal--spectral distance identity
thm:supp-A3-distance.note: sup over vertex pairs of |d_h(x,y) - d_g(x,y)| -> 0 is proved with d_h the actual finite commutator-supremum Connes distance and d_g the flat quotient metric of W_0/Lambda_{A3}. Scoped: d_g is taken as the flat lattice quotient metric directly; the paper's identification of that metric with the second-moment reconstruction is not part of the Lean statement.

lem:positive-stencil-main.title: Positive local stencil
lem:positive-stencil-main.note: Proved. (a) Near-identity clause: every symmetric matrix entrywise within eta <= 1/d of the identity lies in the stencil window and admits the positive d^2-direction decomposition with the explicit weights (positive_stencil_of_nearOne, on top of positive_stencil_decomposition). (b) Linear normalization at a point: every positive definite real matrix P has an invertible S with S P S^T = 1 (exists_normalization, via the spectral theorem). (c) Good-cover clause: for a continuous field of positive definite matrices on a compact space (the inverse metric of a closed Riemannian manifold) there is a finite family of open charts with linear normalizations covering the space such that on every chart the normalized field S g(x) S^T lies in the stencil window and has a strictly positive stencil decomposition (exists_finite_positive_stencil_cover). Scoped reformulation disclosed: the manifold is abstracted to a compact topological space carrying a continuous positive definite matrix field; no Riemannian-manifold structure is formalized.

thm:compact-spin-main.title: Norm-resolvent convergence criterion under atlas stability
thm:compact-spin-main.note: Partial: the abstract analytic step of the proof (strong convergence of a collectively compact family and of its adjoints implies operator-norm convergence, with compact limit) is proved; missing: the Wilson operators, the atlas hypotheses, Rellich compactness of embedded resolvents, identification of the limit with (D-z)^{-1}, and the metric-head convergence.
thm:compact-spin-main.plan: Identical to thm:supp-compact-spin-resolvent plus thm:supp-global-metric. Only OperatorLimits/CollectivelyCompactStrongAdjointToNorm.lean:tendsto_operatorNorm_of_collectivelyCompact_of_adjointStrong exists. Missing: Wilson operators, the atlas definition (needs H^1 spinor Sobolev space), Rellich compactness, unbounded self-adjoint D̂ with a smooth core and identification of the strong limit with (D̂ - z)^{-1}, and the geodesic metric convergence; all outside Mathlib's current reach.

def:supp-current-polytope.title: Admissible cycle-current polytope
def:supp-current-polytope.note: SimpleOrientation V E is a simple undirected graph presented by one orientation (tail, head) of each edge (no parallel edges, no antiparallel pair, hence no loops); incidenceReal is the real incidence matrix B : R^E -> R^V, B_{x e} = [tail e = x] - [head e = x], and incidence its complex copy. currentPolytope G c = {j | B j = 0 and |j_e| < c_e for all e} is J(G,c); closedCurrentPolytope is the non-strict closed fibre, with currentPolytope ⊆ closedCurrentPolytope. currentPolytope_eq_fibre identifies J(G,c) with the earlier complex-incidence GraphSpectralFibre via isStationaryCurrent_incidence_iff.

thm:supp-graph-realization.title: Stationary Markov realization fibre of a metric graph triple
thm:supp-graph-realization.note: stationary_markov_realization_fibre (positive masses m, positive edge conductances c, simple graph G): (R1) reversibleRates = c/m is a stationary realization with detailed balance m_x k_xy = m_y k_yx; (R2) every j in J(G,c) gives the stationary realization k = (c+j)/m with strictly positive directed rates on every edge, the stationarity following from sum_y (q_xy - q_yx) = 2 (B j)_x (sum_pairFlux_sub, the missing link of the previous assessment); (R3) every stationary realization with masses m and symmetrized flux equal to c (IsRealization: zero diagonal, nonnegative rates, mass stationarity, (q+q^T)/2 = c on edges and 0 off edges) is uniquely (c+j)/m with j = (q - q^T)/2 in the closed polytope, and in the open polytope J(G,c) exactly when both directed rates of every edge are positive (IsRealization.currentOf_mem); (R4) the Hodge-Dirac matrix dirac m ((q+q^T)/2) of every current realization equals dirac m c (and representation never depends on rates); eq:supp-realization-fibre is the explicit bijection realizationEquiv : J(G,c) ≃ {positive-edge stationary realizations} (closedRealizationEquiv for the closed fibre). IsRealization.toStationaryRenewalGraph / isRealization_of_stationaryRenewalGraph tie realizations to def:supp-renewal-graph and hence to canonical_graph_spectralization. Scoped/disclosed: the graph is simple (the paper's 'up to unread parallel-channel refinements'), the diagonal of k is normalized to 0, and the (R3) uniqueness lands in J(G,c) itself only for realizations with positive directed edge rates (otherwise in the closed fibre, as the paper's definition remarks).

cor:supp-fibre-dimension.title: Dimension and faithfulness of the fibre
cor:supp-fibre-dimension.note: fibre_dimension_and_faithfulness, for a connected simple graph G (SimpleOrientation.Connected = reflexive-transitive closure of adjacency), positive masses and positive edge conductances: (i) the cycle space ker B carrying J(G,c) has complex dimension |E|+1-|V| = b_1(G) (isConnectedIncidence derives the cycle-projector criterion from graph connectedness, then cycleKernel_finrank); (ii) it is zero, i.e. the reversible realization is the unique one, iff |E|+1 = |V| (tree); (iii) if b_1(G) > 0 (|V| < |E|+1) there are two distinct points of J(G,c) — a nonzero kernel vector, obtained from the real or imaginary part of a nonzero complex kernel vector and scaled into the open box (exists_ne_zero_mem_currentPolytope), and 0 — whose stationary realizations differ but have the same Hodge-Dirac matrix dirac m c (spectralization_not_faithful): the metric spectralization is not faithful. Scoped: V nonempty; 'dim J(G,c)' is stated as the dimension of the ambient cycle kernel (J(G,c) is an open neighbourhood of 0 in it, as in the paper's proof).

prop:supp-entropy.title: Entropy production inside one spectral fibre
prop:supp-entropy.note: sigma(j) = 2 sum_e j_e log((c_e+j_e)/(c_e-j_e)) is taken as the definition; nonnegativity and vanishing exactly at j=0 are proved under 0 < c_e and |j_e| < c_e. Scoped: the derivation of this formula from (1/2) sum (q_xy - q_yx) log(q_xy/q_yx) is not compiled.

thm:supp-spectral-universality.title: Finite spectral universality
thm:supp-spectral-universality.note: Proved in the reformulation the paper's proof establishes. For a real oriented incidence matrix of a connected graph with b_1 = |E|-|V|+1 > 0 and positive conductances c: (1) there is a nonzero stationary current j in the same-spectralization fibre whose directed flux data (hence renewal generator) and entropy production differ from the reversible member j = 0 while both share the symmetrized flux c, i.e. the same metric spectral triple; (2) the fibre equals the open conductance box intersected with the real cycle space ker B, it is a star-shaped neighbourhood of 0 in that space, the real cycle space has dimension b_1 (finrank_realCycleSpace, derived from the complex cycle-kernel dimension via the real/imaginary-part isomorphism), and distinct currents give distinct generators (forwardFlux_injective). Disclosed gap: 'dynamically inequivalent' is formalised as distinct generators with equal spectral data plus the entropy-production witness against the reversible member; pairwise non-isomorphism of two arbitrary nonzero currents up to vertex relabelling is not what the paper's proof establishes and is not claimed.

lem:supp-zero-affinity.title: Zero affinity class forces reversibility
lem:supp-zero-affinity.note: Proved in the paper's generality: for a real oriented incidence matrix B : Matrix V E ℝ (finite V, E) and conductances c, a current j in the fibre (B j = 0 and |j_e| < c_e) whose affinity a_e = Real.artanh (j_e / c_e) is exact (a = Bᵀ φ for some vertex potential φ, i.e. [a] = 0 in ℝ^E / Ran Bᵀ) is zero. Proof pairs φ against B j to get Σ_e a_e j_e = 0, each term nonnegative and vanishing only at j_e = 0 (Real.artanh_nonneg/nonpos/eq_zero_iff). Connectedness is not needed for this conclusion (a = Bᵀφ = 0 already forces j = 0 edgewise).

thm:supp-nonlinear-Hodge.title: Nonlinear Hodge theorem for stationary affinities
thm:supp-nonlinear-Hodge.note: Proved for a real incidence matrix B with the connected-incidence hypotheses Bᵀ1 = 0 and ker Bᵀ = constants (IsConnectedIncidence) and positive conductances: the affinity functional F_α(φ) = Σ c_e log cosh(a₀_e + (Bᵀφ)_e) has a unique mean-zero minimiser φ_α; a_α = a₀ + Bᵀφ_α and j_α = c tanh a_α satisfy B j_α = 0, |j_α| < c, artanh(j_α/c) = a_α, [a_α] = α, and j_α is the unique fibre current of class α; the affinity map 𝔄 : 𝒥(G,c) → H¹(G;ℝ) = ℝ^E / Ran Bᵀ is a bijection (Set.BijOn onto the quotient). Coercivity is proved as F_α(φ) + (Σφ)² → ∞ along the cocompact filter. Not formalised: strict convexity of F_α (uniqueness is derived from the Euler equation plus strict monotonicity of tanh instead) and the smoothness of 𝔄⁻¹ (the word 'diffeomorphism'); the bijection and explicit inverse formulas are proved. The real hypotheses IsConnectedIncidence B are derived from the repo's complex predicate RenewalGeometry.IsConnectedIncidence (B.map ofReal) (isConnectedIncidence_of_complex) and hence from graph connectedness of a SimpleOrientation (isConnectedIncidence_incidenceReal); existsUnique_current_of_connected states the bijection clause directly for a connected graph's real incidence matrix.

cor:supp-faithful-modular.title: Faithful metric--modular enrichment
cor:supp-faithful-modular.note: Proved directly, bypassing thm:supp-nonlinear-Hodge: two currents in the fibre 𝒥(G,c) whose affinities differ by an exact cochain (same class [a] in H^1 = ℝ^E / Ran Bᵀ) coincide (strict monotonicity of artanh via Real.artanh_le_artanh_iff / artanh_injOn); hence for fixed (G,m,c) the class [a] determines the directed fluxes q = c ± j (forwardFlux/reverseFlux) and the stationary rates k_xy = q_xy/m_x (forwardRate/reverseRate of FiniteGraphSpectralUniversalityFibre, eq. supp-current-realization). The metric packet (C(V),H_{m,c},D_{m,c},J,γ) depends on (G,m,c) only, so this is the faithfulness claim. The explicit inverse a_α (minimiser of the convex functional of thm:supp-nonlinear-Hodge) is not constructed here; only the injectivity the corollary asserts.

thm:supp-Tomita.title: Finite modular-reversal identities
thm:supp-Tomita.note: All identities of eq:supp-Tomita-identities and eq:supp-Tomita-opposite proved pointwise on ℓ²(E^or) = (Eor → ℂ), with E^or modelled as a type with an involutive reversal bar, source s, terminal t = s ∘ bar, and positive fluxes q: J_E² = I; J_E Δ_q J_E = Δ_q⁻¹ (explicit multiplier q_{ē}/q_e plus the two-sided inverse identity); S_q² = I; J_E λ_E(f*) J_E = ρ_E(f); S_q λ_E(f*) S_q = ρ_E(f) (S_q = S_q⁻¹ since S_q² = I); log Δ_q(e) = 2 a_e with a_e = ½ log(q_e/q_{ē}), shown equal to artanh(j_e/c_e) when q_e = c_e + j_e, q_{ē} = c_e − j_e; a_{ē} = −a_e; reversible branch Δ_q = I ↔ q_e = q_{ē} for all e. Not stated separately: antiunitarity (ℓ² isometry) of J_E, which is only used in the paper's proof, not in the statement.

thm:supp-modular-Hodge.title: Cellular modular Hodge reconstruction
thm:supp-modular-Hodge.note: Proved for an arbitrary finite real Hilbert complex d₀,d₁,d₂ (finite-dimensional real inner product spaces, d₁d₀ = 0, d₂d₁ = 0) with ℋ¹ = ker d₁ ⊓ ker d₀* and h_a = P_{ℋ¹} a, F_a = d₁ a: existence and uniqueness of the orthogonal decomposition a = d₀φ + h_a + d₁*ψ; coexact reconstruction P_{Ran d₁*} a = d₁* G F_a; injectivity of [a] ↦ (h_a, F_a) (equal data ⇒ a - b ∈ Ran d₀) and surjectivity onto ℋ¹ ⊕ Ran d₁ via the canonical representative a_{h,F} = h + d₁* G F; Bianchi d₂F_a = 0; norm identity ‖a‖² = ‖d₀φ‖² + ‖h_a‖² + ⟪F_a, G F_a⟫. Scope disclosed: (d₁d₁*)† is modelled by any generalised inverse G with (d₁d₁*) G (d₁d₁*) = d₁d₁* (the Moore–Penrose inverse is one; existence is proved by spectralGeneralizedInverse, which inverts the nonzero eigenvalues in an orthonormal eigenbasis); all displayed formulas are independent of the choice of G.

cor:supp-modular-trichotomy.title: Flat, globally twisted, and curved modular branches
cor:supp-modular-trichotomy.note: Proved. Clauses (M1)-(M3) are CellularModularHodge.modular_trichotomy (case split on F_a = d1 a and h_a = P_{H^1} a, with a = d0 phi in the flat sector), derived from the proved parent thm:supp-modular-Hodge (cellular_modular_hodge). The three-torus clause is proved on the cubical cochain complex of the periodic n x n x n lattice (vertices (Z/n)^3, edges vertex x axis, faces vertex x {i<j}, d0 phi(v,i) = phi(v+e_i) - phi(v), d1 a(v,i,j) = a(v,i) + a(v+e_i,j) - a(v+e_j,i) - a(v,j), Euclidean inner products): d1 d0 = 0, the explicit adjoint d0* a(v) = sum_i (a(v-e_i,i) - a(v,i)), and finrank H^1 = 3 (finrank_harmonicSpace_eq_three) via the energy identity: a harmonic one-cochain has translation-invariant, hence constant, axis components, so H^1 is the span of the three axis-constant cochains (modular_trichotomy_three_torus packages both clauses). Scoped hypothesis: period n >= 1 (NeZero n); the model is the standard cubical complex of the discrete three-torus.

thm:supp-face-holonomy.title: Face holonomy
thm:supp-face-holonomy.note: Proved: for signed face-incidence coefficients ε_{p,e} ∈ ℤ (the cellular coboundary d_1, so F_a(p) = Σ_e ε_{p,e} a_e is the definition of faceCurvature), Π_e (q_e/q_{ē})^{ε_{p,e}} = exp(2 F_a(p)) with a_e = ½ log(q_e/q_{ē}) and 0 < q_e; descent criterion: all face holonomies equal 1 iff all face-curvature residuals vanish. The same lemma gives eq:supp-modular-cycle-holonomy with ε the oriented-cycle indicator. F_a is encoded through its coboundary formula rather than an abstract Hilbert-complex d_1.

def:supp-POVM.title: Positive operator-valued tail measure
def:supp-POVM.note: Encoded: a bounded positive operator-valued tail measure on (0,∞) for finite-dimensional H is a Mathlib VectorMeasure ℝ (H → H → ℂ) (product topology, so countable additivity is entrywise = weak = norm in finite dimension) whose values on measurable sets are positive semidefinite and which vanishes on Borel subsets of (-∞,0]; boundedness of μ((0,∞)) is automatic. The Stieltjes self-energy Σ_μ(z) = ∫ (λ - z)⁻¹ dμ(λ) is Mathlib's vector-measure integral (VectorMeasure.integral) of the scalar function against μ paired through scalar multiplication ℂ × B(H) → B(H); the Euclidean memory kernel and the moments M_n are defined the same way. The atoms λ Q δ_λ are instantiated (atomic) and their self-energy computed.

con:supp-Naimark-tail.title: Canonical minimal Stieltjes dilation
con:supp-Naimark-tail.note: Partial: the finite-outcome Naimark dilation (stacked square-root isometry and coordinate projections) is constructed; missing: the simple-function Hilbert space K_mu, the projection-valued measure P_mu, C_mu = int lambda dP_mu and B_mu = V_mu^* for a Borel operator measure.
con:supp-Naimark-tail.plan: Requires the Hilbert-space completion of H-valued simple functions under ⟨·,·⟩_μ (equivalently L^2(Tr μ; H) with the matrix-density weight ρ = dμ/dTr μ), the projection-valued measure P_μ(E) = multiplication by 1_E, and the unbounded self-adjoint multiplication operator C_μ = ∫ λ dP_μ on an unbounded support. Mathlib has L^2 spaces and MeasureTheory.Lp but no spectral-measure calculus or unbounded multiplication operators packaged as self-adjoint operators; infrastructure-level. A bounded-support version (C_μ bounded, K_μ = Lp with weighted inner product) is a large but finite-analysis project.

thm:supp-Naimark-realization.title: Operator-measure realization and minimality
thm:supp-Naimark-realization.note: Partial: for a finite-outcome POVM the dilation is isometric, the outcomes are orthogonal projections resolving one, and compression recovers every effect; missing: the resolvent identity Sigma_mu(z) = B(C-z)^{-1}B^*, the minimality span, the converse from (C,B) and the unique intertwining unitary between minimal realizations.
thm:supp-Naimark-realization.plan: Depends on con:supp-Naimark-tail. Needs the resolvent of the unbounded multiplication operator C_μ, the identity Σ_μ(z) = B_μ (C_μ - z)^{-1} B_μ^*, minimality of the cyclic span, the converse from a spectral measure E_C (spectral theorem for unbounded self-adjoint operators, absent from Mathlib) and uniqueness of the intertwining unitary between minimal realizations. Only the finite-outcome case is proved (FiniteNaimarkDilation.lean:finiteNaimarkDilation), where it could be stated as: for finite atomic μ = Σ Q_i δ_{λ_i}, Σ_μ(z) = B (C - z)^{-1} B^* with C = diag(λ_i) — that finite-atomic version would be medium.

thm:supp-dynamic-jets.title: Static shadows, inverse moments, and positive Euclidean memory
thm:supp-dynamic-jets.note: Partial: the Herglotz sign is proved in the finite atomic case (Im of the matrix Stieltjes transform is a Poisson-kernel weighted sum of psd spectral weights), and the zero-mass response int lambda^{-1} dSigma and Euclidean memory int e^{-t lambda} dSigma are defined for scalar measures with scaling laws; missing: general operator measures, the inverse-moment boundary jets, and the Laplace relation Sigma(-s) = int e^{-st} K(t) dt.
thm:supp-dynamic-jets.plan: As stated for general operator measures it needs def:supp-POVM plus dominated convergence for entrywise integrals, the inverse-moment boundary jets (r-th derivative of s ↦ ∫ (λ + s)^{-1} dμ under the integral sign) and the Laplace/Fubini relation Σ_μ(-s) = ∫_0^∞ e^{-st} K_μ(t) dt (MeasureTheory.integral_prod / Fubini with e^{-t(λ+s)}). Mathlib has the scalar tools (integral_Ioi_exp_neg, hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le), but the operator-measure layer is missing. The finite-atomic case (already partially in Miscellany/AssortedFiniteRecords03.lean:ResistanceClock) reduces every clause to finite sums and would be medium.

thm:supp-memory-determinacy.title: Determinacy on controlled support
thm:supp-memory-determinacy.note: Proved, both clauses, on the def:supp-POVM encoding PositiveTailMeasure (countably additive B(H)-valued Borel measure on R vanishing on (-inf,0], PSD values, H finite). Compact clause (eq_of_isSupportedIn_of_moment_eq): mu, mu' supported in (0,R] (IsSupportedIn R; bounded support suffices) with moment mu n = moment mu' n for all n implies mu = mu'. Exponential clause (eq_of_integrable_exp_traceMeasure_of_moment_eq): if exp(a x) is integrable for the trace measure E |-> Re Tr mu(E) (traceMeasure, a > 0) for both measures, equal moments imply mu = mu'. Packaged as memory_determinacy. Proof: scalarise along the quadratic forms xi |-> Re<xi, mu(.) xi> (formMeasure, a finite positive measure; the operator moment scalarises to the scalar moment via the bridge quadFormCLM_moment, which needs finiteness of the variation of mu, obtained from the PSD entry bound |M_ij| <= Re Tr M and domination of the variation by the trace measure); scalar determinacy (measure_eq_of_forall_integral_pow_eq) via the complex moment generating function: analytic on Re z < a, Taylor coefficients at 0 are the moments, identity theorem on the half-plane, characteristic functions agree, Measure.ext_of_charFun; the compact case is the special case a = 1; polarisation (matrix_eq_zero_of_forall_quadForm_eq_zero) recovers the operator measure from its quadratic forms. Scoped choices: 'supp mu compact' is encoded as support in (0,R] for some R; 'int e^{a lambda} dTr mu < infinity' as Integrable (exp (a x)) traceMeasure.

cth:supp-moment-indeterminate.title: All integer moments can miss the dynamic self-energy
cth:supp-moment-indeterminate.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: lognormal, sin(2 pi log x), indeterminate, Stieltjes transform injectivity. Together research-level effort inside Mathlib's reach only with substantial work.

thm:supp-contact-escape.title: High-energy memory escape and instantaneous contact terms
thm:supp-contact-escape.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: escape, one-point compactification, weak-* compactness, contact term, delta_0, tail measure. NCG/Grand/EscapeHeadConcentrationExact.lean concerns finite operator escape estimates of a different theorem.

cth:supp-contact-static.title: The static triple does not identify escaped memory
cth:supp-contact-static.note: Proved for the atoms μ_n = λ_n Q δ_{λ_n} (Q ⪰ 0, λ_n > 0, λ_n → ∞) with the def:supp-POVM encoding: Σ_n(0) = Q, Σ_n(z) = λ_n/(λ_n - z) Q → Q for every z ∈ ℂ (in particular off [0,∞)), K_n(t) = λ_n e^{-λ_n t} Q → 0 for every t > 0, and the distributional convergence K_n(t)dt → Q δ_0 in the form ∫_0^∞ φ(t) λ_n e^{-λ_n t} dt · Q → φ(0) Q for every bounded continuous test function φ on ℝ (which covers C_c([0,∞)) test functions); the approximate-identity lemma is proved by the substitution t = s/λ_n and dominated convergence.

def:supp-marked-spectral-packet.title: Marked spectral packet
def:supp-marked-spectral-packet.note: Encoded: a marked finite spectral packet bundles a CoordinateFiniteRealEvenSpectralPacket (𝒜,ℋ,D,J,γ in orthonormal coordinates), declared marking data 𝔪 (an element of an arbitrary type carrying a MulAction of the unitary group of the carrier, so 'preserved by a unitary' means 'stabilised'), and a declared algebra automorphism convention (pointwise fixing or setwise normalising the represented algebra; both proved to be subgroups). G_S = Aut(S) is defined as the Subgroup of Matrix.unitaryGroup K ℂ of unitaries commuting with D, γ, J (packetAutomorphisms, proved closed under 1, mul, inv), satisfying the convention, and stabilising 𝔪. Not proved: compactness of G_S; it is not used by thm:supp-character-shadow.

thm:supp-marked-bundle.title: Marked spectral-bundle descent
thm:supp-marked-bundle.note: Proved for an arbitrary group Gamma in the role of G_S = Aut(S) (vertex packets identified with the reference packet, so edge maps are elements of Gamma with U(bar e) = U(e)^{-1} built into backward traversal) on any NCG.Multigraph connected to the base vertex v0. (B1): the walk holonomy (ordered product of edge labels) is multiplicative under concatenation, unital, inverts under reversal and is backtracking invariant, hence is the monodromy homomorphism on pi_1(Gamma, v0) presented as closed walks modulo backtracking; (B2): a frame change g conjugates every loop holonomy by the single element g(v0); (B3): a global marked trivialisation (frame change making every edge map the identity) exists iff all loop holonomies are 1; (B4): two bundle data are gauge equivalent iff their loop holonomies at v0 are conjugate by one element (the clutching classification Hom(pi_1, G_S)/G_S). Reformulation disclosed: pi_1 is presented by closed walks (not as the free group on chords of a spanning tree), so the remark that the bundle is determined by b_1 elements of G_S modulo conjugation is not formalised; compactness of G_S is not used.

cor:supp-twisted-bundle.title: Nontrivial monodromy is a twisted geometry
cor:supp-twisted-bundle.note: Proved as the contrapositive of (B3): with 'flat twisted spectral geometry' defined as a flat bundle datum admitting no global marked trivialisation (IsFlatTwisted), a nontrivial monodromy (some closed walk with holonomy != 1, equivalently a nontrivial conjugacy class [rho_U], monodromy_class_trivial_iff) forces the geometry to be twisted; the compatibility relation U(bar e) = U(e)^{-1} is built into the walk holonomy. Same modelling disclosures as thm:supp-marked-bundle.

thm:supp-character-shadow.title: Line characters are incomplete shadows of frame holonomy
thm:supp-character-shadow.note: Proved: (i) trivial frame holonomy ρ = 1 forces every induced character holonomy χ_j ∘ ρ, ε_k ∘ ρ to be trivial (arbitrary groups); (ii) if ⋂_j Ker χ_j ∩ ⋂_k Ker ε_k = {1} then trivial character holonomies force ρ = 1 for every monodromy ρ from any group; (iii) the 'exactly when': for monodromies of the free fundamental group π_1(Γ) = FreeGroup β on b_1(Γ) ≥ 1 generators (Nonempty β), the characters detect every frame holonomy iff the joint kernel is trivial (the paper's one-cycle construction, via FreeGroup.lift). Specialised to G_S = autGroup of a marked packet with U(1)-valued characters (Circle) and Pfaffian-sign characters (ℤˣ). Scoped hypotheses: b_1 ≥ 1 for the 'only if' direction (for b_1 = 0 every ρ is trivial and the criterion is vacuous); π_1(Γ) is taken as the abstract free group of rank b_1, as in the paper; the graph monodromy ρ_U of thm:supp-marked-bundle is an arbitrary homomorphism here.

cth:supp-det-no-frame.title: A trivial determinant line need not trivialize the packet
cth:supp-det-no-frame.note: Concrete SU(2) computation. g = diagonal ![exp(iθ), exp(-iθ)] : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ has det g = 1, lies in Matrix.unitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ (the marked automorphism group U(2) of a scalar-algebra, zero-Dirac, multiplicity-two packet), commutes with D = 0 and with every scalar c•1, and g ≠ 1 when θ ≠ 2πn for all n : ℤ. The one-cycle graph has π₁ = Multiplicative ℤ; oneCycleMonodromy θ = zpowersHom g is the marked monodromy, its composite with the determinant character detCharacter : U(2) →* ℂˣ is the trivial homomorphism (trivial determinant-line holonomy), while oneCycleMonodromy θ ≠ 1 for θ ∉ 2πℤ (nontrivial marked bundle monodromy, via thm:supp-marked-bundle (B3)). Scoped choice disclosed: the marked automorphism group is modelled as the full unitary group U(2) ⊇ SU(2) of the packet's Hilbert carrier, and π₁ of the one-cycle graph as Multiplicative ℤ.

thm:supp-current-chain.title: Current-chain functor
thm:supp-current-chain.note: Proved over R for finite oriented graphs (tail/head maps, multi-edges allowed) and a vertex quotient q : V -> V-bar with induced coarse graph in which every fine edge is either mapped to a coarse edge with the quotient endpoints or is internal to a fibre and dropped (VertexQuotient); Q_V, Q_E are the fibre-summation matrices. (i) chain identity d-bar Q_E = Q_V d as a matrix identity, hence Q_E Z(G) <= Z(G-bar); (ii) Q_E Curr(G,c) <= Curr(G-bar, c-bar) with c-bar = Q_E c, under the hypothesis that every coarse edge has a nonempty fibre ('retains every inter-fibre edge class', needed for the strict inequality); (iii) with connected fibres (through internal edges) and retained classes, Q_E : Z(G) -> Z(G-bar) is onto (constructive lift: one representative per coarse edge, divergence completed by internal path flows), so the short sequence is exact and dim ker = dim Z(G) - dim Z(G-bar); with G and G-bar connected and nonempty this is (|E|-|V|+1) - (|E-bar|-|V-bar|+1) via a real Betti-number lemma; (iv) sigma_{G-bar}(Q_E j) <= sigma_G(j) for j in the open polytope with c > 0, via the log-sum inequality (sum_rateDivergence_ge_total) applied to forward/reverse fluxes c +- j on each coarse-edge fibre. Scoped hypotheses disclosed: finiteness, Nonempty V / V-bar and connectedness of both graphs for the Betti form of the kernel dimension.

thm:supp-memory-RG.title: Exact memory RG semigroup
thm:supp-memory-RG.note: Proved for the general weakly countably additive measure of def:supp-POVM (PositiveTailMeasure; Stieltjes integrals are Mathlib vector-measure integrals), in the L2 operator norm on Matrix H H C, with F_{A,mu}(z) = A - z - Sigma_mu(z), Q_{>Lambda} = int_{(Lambda,inf)} lambda^{-1} dmu, mu|_{(0,Lambda]} = restriction to Iic Lambda, RG_Lambda(A,mu) = (A - Q_{>Lambda}, mu|_{(0,Lambda]}). (1) eq:supp-memory-static-preserved (dynamicFunction_rg_zero): F_{RG}(0) = F(0) under the hypothesis that lambda^{-1} is mu-integrable, i.e. exactly that the static value F_{A,mu}(0) exists (the paper's implicit assumption; without it both sides are the Lean convention value and the identity is false). (2) eq:supp-memory-screen-error (norm_dynamicFunction_sub_rg_le): for ||z|| <= r < Lambda and z outside [0,inf) (the domain of the Stieltjes self-energy in def:supp-POVM), ||F(z) - F_{RG}(z)|| <= r/(Lambda - r) ||Q_{>Lambda}||, no integrability hypothesis needed; the variant _of_integrable takes instead the integrability of (lambda - z)^{-1}. The analytic core is the positive-weighted operator-norm bound for operator integrals l2_opNorm_integral_le_of_norm_le (||int c dmu|| <= kappa ||int w dmu|| when |c| <= kappa w a.e., w >= 0), proved by scalarising along the sesquilinear complex measures <x, mu(.) y>, dominating their total variation by (t/2)<x,mu x> + (1/(2t))<y,mu y> via the PSD Cauchy-Schwarz inequality posSemidef_norm_sesqForm_le, integrating and optimising in t. (3) eq:supp-memory-semigroup (rg_rg): RG_{Lambda2} o RG_{Lambda1} = RG_{Lambda2} for 0 < Lambda2 <= Lambda1 (head corrections add over the disjoint shells, cutoffs compose). Packaged in memory_rg_semigroup. The finite atomic special case remains in MemoryCutoffSemigroupExact (its scalar tail estimate norm_inv_sub_inv_le is reused).

thm:supp-monodromy-descent.title: Exact marked-monodromy descent
thm:supp-monodromy-descent.note: Abstract group-theoretic form, with π₁(Γ), π₁(Γ̄), G_S arbitrary groups and q_* any surjective homomorphism (the graph-contraction origin of q_* is not modelled; the theorem only uses surjectivity). monodromy_descends_iff: (∃! ρ̄, ρ = ρ̄ ∘ q_*) ↔ ker q_* ≤ ker ρ. monodromyDescent is the descended ρ̄ with monodromyDescent_comp (factorisation) and monodromyDescent_unique. Gauge independence: monodromyDescent_conj shows conjugating ρ by g ∈ G_S conjugates ρ̄ by the same g, so [ρ̄] is gauge independent. Functoriality: monodromyDescent_comp_surjective shows descent along q₁ then q₂ equals descent along q₂ ∘ q₁. Character remark: ker_le_ker_character_comp (a character of a descending ρ descends) and detCharacter_descends_but_monodromy_does_not (the one-cycle SU(2) example of cth:supp-det-no-frame: collapsing the cycle to a point, the determinant character satisfies the descended kernel condition while the full marked monodromy does not).

lem:supp-positive-decomposition.title: Positive $d^2$-direction decomposition
lem:supp-positive-decomposition.note: Index type is any finite linearly ordered type ι (Fin d in the paper), d = Fintype.card ι, matrices over ℝ. Hypotheses: A symmetric (Matrix.IsSymm), η > 0, |A i j| < η for i ≠ j, (d-1)η < A i i. positive_stencil_decomposition gives strict positivity of w_i = A i i - (d-1)η, w⁺_ij = (η + A i j)/2, w⁻_ij = (η - A i j)/2 (the latter two for i ≠ j) and the identity A = Σ_i w_i e_i e_iᵀ + Σ_i Σ_j stencilPairTerm i j, where stencilPairTerm i j = w⁺_ij (e_i+e_j)(e_i+e_j)ᵀ + w⁻_ij (e_i-e_j)(e_i-e_j)ᵀ for i < j and 0 otherwise (so the double sum is exactly the paper's Σ_{i<j}). thm:supp-general-renewal-process.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: coframe renewal process, predictable bracket, Laplace-Beltrami, Dirichlet form convergence, reversible packet on h Z^d.

lem:supp-density-symmetric.note: No Lean counterpart found; searched: density symmetric, rho^{1/2}, sqrt det g, spin connection, Clifford contraction.

thm:supp-compact-spin-resolvent.title: Norm-resolvent convergence for compatible stable atlases
thm:supp-compact-spin-resolvent.note: Partial: the compactness upgrade used in the proof (a collectively compact sequence converging strongly together with its adjoints converges in operator norm, with compact limit) is proved for a fixed Hilbert space; missing: the atlas hypotheses (A1)-(A3), Rellich compactness of the embedded resolvents, identification of the limit as (D-z)^{-1} via the smooth core, the periodic-extension statement and the spectral-projection consequences.
thm:supp-compact-spin-resolvent.plan: The norm upgrade is proved (OperatorLimits/CollectivelyCompactStrongAdjointToNorm.lean). Missing: strong resolvent convergence from the core condition (A3), which needs an unbounded self-adjoint D̂ with domain, its resolvent, and the argument 'weak limit of R_h(z) f satisfies (D̂ - z)u = f distributionally hence u = R(z) f' — unbounded operator theory not in Mathlib; Rellich compactness of embedded resolvents from (A1)-(A2) needs the compact embedding H^1 → L^2 (abstractable as a hypothesis, see def:stable-spin-atlas); spectral-projection convergence needs Riesz projections. Hard even in the abstract surrogate because of the unbounded self-adjoint limit.

def:supp-rational-Hermitian.title: Normalized rational Hermitian dynamic function
def:supp-rational-Hermitian.note: Encoded: Q is represented by its Hermitian Laurent coefficients M_n at infinity (eq:supp-rational-Laurent; Q(z-bar)^* = Q(z) is coeff_symmetric, Q(infinity)=0 is strict properness of the expansion) with rationality encoded, per Kronecker, as finite Hankel rank (finiteRank); laurentDynamicFunction is the series -sum M_n z^{-n-1}. Hankel columns c_j(h), their span K_Q, the sesquilinear Hankel form with [c_i(u), c_j(v)] = <u, M_{i+j} v> (hankelForm_single_single), its null space, the quotient state space with the descended form (hankelStateForm), A_Q c_j = c_{j+1} (hankelShift, well-defined by hankelFormalShift_null_le) and Gamma_Q h = c_0(h) (hankelSource). Proved in addition: the null space equals the kernel of the formal-to-literal column map for Hermitian coefficients (hankelNull_eq_ker), so the quotient is canonically the literal column span (hankelStateEquivColumnSpace), and [A^i Gamma u, A^j Gamma v] = <u, M_{i+j} v>. Not encoded: the equivalence rational-function <-> finite Hankel rank (Kronecker) and the identification of the tsum with the rational function.

thm:supp-complete-rational-Krein.plan: Beyond the definite Hankel realization (operatorHankel_minimalRealizations_uniquelySimilar, finiteOperatorHankelRank_realization): needs the resolvent identity Q(z) = Γ^+ (A - z)^{-1} Γ as an identity of rational functions from the Laurent coefficients, the Pontryagin (indefinite) inner product on the quotient with negative index = inertia of the Hankel form (Krein/SignedHaynsworthInertia.lean supplies Sylvester inertia), the count of negative squares of the Nevanlinna kernel N_Q(z,w), and uniqueness up to a source-fixing Pontryagin unitary. Research-level finite indefinite realization theory (Krein-Langer) with no library support beyond inertia; hard.

thm:supp-common-source.title: Joint Gram classification
thm:supp-common-source.note: Proved in finite dimensions with E_a = C^{n a} (index types in Type, as required by the reused repo lemma source_kernel_realization_minimal_unique) and X = Sigma a, n a. Corr_X = {K psd, K_aa = I} (CorrelationSpectrahedron); G_X = Pi_a U(n a) acting by block congruence K -> D(g)^H K D(g) (gaugeAct), which preserves Corr_X (block_gaugeAct, gaugeAct_mem_corr); Stab(K) is a Subgroup (stabilizer). A joint realization of K on a common space C^C is S : Matrix C X with S^H S = K (columns over block a = images of the marginal basis), its realization space Ran S. Proved: the Gram of a realization lies in Corr_X iff its marginal blocks are identities (isometric V_a); every K in Corr_X is realized (by sqrt K) with rank = rank K; every realization's Ran S has dimension exactly rank K and rank K <= dim of the common space (rank K is the minimum joint realization dimension, attained by restricting to Ran S); two realizations are equivalent up to a marginal frame change g and a source-fixing isometric identification of the realization spaces iff their Grams lie in the same G_X-orbit (frameUnitaryEquivalent_iff; the identification is unique, exists_unique_range_unitary, via the repo's joint_source_unique_range_unitary); for a realization S of K, a frame change g is implemented by such a unitary on Ran S iff g in Stab(K) (mem_stabilizer_iff_residual). Modelling disclosure: 'unitary on the common realization space' is formalised as a source-fixing linear equivalence between the ranges preserving the ambient inner product (the repo's convention), and 'minimal' as restriction to Ran S.

cth:supp-pairwise-not-global.title: Pairwise positivity need not give a joint realization
cth:supp-pairwise-not-global.note: The explicit 3×3 real matrix M = !![1,-3/4,-3/4; -3/4,1,-3/4; -3/4,-3/4,1]: M *ᵥ (1,1,1) = (-1/2)•(1,1,1), hence Module.End.HasEigenvalue (Matrix.toLin' M) (-1/2); M is not Matrix.PosSemidef (quadratic form -3/2 on (1,1,1)); and for every i ≠ j in Fin 3 the principal block M.submatrix ![i,j] ![i,j] is Matrix.PosDef (all blocks equal !![1,-3/4;-3/4,1], whose form is (x₀ - 3x₁/4)² + 7x₁²/16). So pairwise-admissible Gram blocks need not assemble into a positive joint Gram operator.
